cases.name: Bethany "Pavitra" Maclaren
cases.about: The Colorado-based Nepali community said they believe Bethany (Pavrita) was actually from India, with some Nepali descendants, and they don't believe she had local family.
cases.narrative: An autopsy report stated Bethany died from six chop wounds. He killed her and her daughter with an ax, partially dismembered them, then stuffed their bodies into individual trash cans in their Englewood, Colo., living room. He admitted to striking his wife in the head with an ax while she was sitting on a couch around 11 a.m. that day. He then said he struck his wife and daughter in the head twice more each before using a saw to sever their arms and legs, because he knew their bodies wouldn’t otherwise fit in the two new trash cans he had recently purchased.

cases.name: Tracy Lee Bloch Lechner
cases.about:
At her funeral, her father said she homeschooled them during the pandemic and read to them every night all while working late at night on her law practice. He called her a woman of valor who visited the sick and made meals for friends, and taught her children to be kind to others.

Her mom spoke at her funeral and said she was an abused woman and had unbridled fear of losing her children while trying to navigate a broken family court system on a daily basis. She described the abuse of women in a court system designed to nullify their complaints. She spoke of PREs - parental rights evaluators with no training in abuse who charge large sums to families, and no one checks on their credentials, and Tracy had done research on them. She spoke of many judges and lawyers who are not trained to recognize abuse, and she said Tracy wanted to change the system and make a difference. Her mother said she always made home-cooked meals and kept kosher.
cases.narrative: She was found deceased on a driveway.
